title: flumph
description: explain the lore and ecology of the dnd flumph, as well as the publication history

script.draft:
Here is the complete video script:

---

[VISUAL: A lone, glowing jellyfish-like creature drifts through pitch-black caverns, tentacles swaying, eyestalks scanning the dark — soft painterly style]

The Underdark is full of monsters that want to kill you. The flumph just wants to be your friend.

Designed by Ian McDowall and Douglas Naismith, the flumph first appeared in D&D's 1981 Fiend Folio. It was the *only* Lawful Good creature in that entire book. A saucer-shaped, air-propelled little weirdo — named after the characteristic sound made by its air jets.

[VISUAL: Close-up cross-section diagram of a flumph — eyestalks, tentacles, spines, glowing mood colors — labeled, retro-illustration style]

Flumphs feed on psionic energy, and are drawn to strong sources — like aboleth, gith, and mind flayer settlements. That's right: they *live* next to the worst creatures in existence, by choice. Their strong telepathic nature makes them sensitive to evil thoughts, and they desperately seek good-aligned creatures to share those thoughts with — just to wash them away.

They organize into cooperative groups called "cloisters," with ordinary members called "monks," led by an "abbot." The inside of a cloister is decorated with fine paintings, made by flumphs dabbing natural pigments with their tentacles.

In the 1988 adventure Castle Greyhawk, flumphs were exiled to the "Plane of Silly and Unused Monsters." A joke — but they survived it. In 2014, Wizards of the Coast confirmed the flumph for the 5th Edition Monster Manual, fully rehabilitated. Lawful Good. Telepathic. Absolutely ridiculous. And completely irreplaceable.

script.description: The flumph is a floating, jellyfish-like creature from the Underdark — and somehow, it's one of the most wholesome beings in all of D&D. In this video, we cover the flumph's strange ecology, its telepathic society, and its wild publication history from the 1981 Fiend Folio all the way to 5th Edition. If you enjoyed this bite-sized lore drop, subscribe for more D&D monster deep-dives every week.
